detailed_description: Docker Run to Docker Compose Converter turns a single docker run command into starter Compose YAML. It parses common flags such as --name, -p/--publish, -e/--env, -v/--volume, --restart, and --network, then writes service name, image, ports, environment, volumes, restart, network_mode, and command fields for review.
usage_steps: Paste the docker run command you want to translate.
Review the generated service name, image, ports, environment variables, volumes, restart policy, and command array.
Add unsupported flags, secrets, health checks, or multi-service wiring manually in your Compose file.
Run your own Docker Compose validation before using the YAML in a real environment.
usage_examples: Convert a one-off container command into a Compose service for local development notes.
Move published ports, environment variables, and volume mounts from a README command into YAML.
Create a starter Compose service, not a complete production deployment, before adding project-specific settings.

faqs.question: Is Docker Run to Docker Compose Converter free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Docker Run to Docker Compose Converter runs free in your browser and does not require an account.

faqs.question: Does it run or validate Docker containers?
faqs.answer: No. It only converts text into starter Compose YAML. Validate the result with Docker Compose in your own environment.

faqs.question: Which docker run flags are recognized?
faqs.answer: The parser handles common name, port, environment, volume, restart, network, image, and command fields. More advanced Docker flags should be added manually.

faqs.question: Can it convert a full multi-container setup?
faqs.answer: No. It converts one docker run command at a time, so multi-service Compose files still need manual design.
